chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Kufi, from Ubays ibn Hisham, from Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad Al-Minqari, from Yunus ibn Zabyan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Indeed, for you is a light by which you are recognized in the world, to the extent that when one of you meets his brother, he kisses him in the place of the light from his forehead.

key_terms.مَوْضِعِ النُّورِ: The place of the light (specific location on the forehead)

ai.seo_question: What is the sign of light on the forehead of the Shia according to Hadith al-Kafi?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) highlights the 'Nur' (light) as a tangible spiritual marker distinguishing the faithful in the material world, facilitating immediate recognition and affectionate greeting among believers. This physical manifestation of inner piety underscores the unity of the spiritual and physical realms in Shia eschatology and identity. The practice of kissing the forehead reflects both reverence for this divine light and the deep communal bonds of the Ahl al-Bayt's followers.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Kufy, from Ubeys Bin Hisham, from Al Husayn Bin Ahmad Al Minqary, from Yunus Bin Zabyan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘For you all (Shia) there is a light you are being recognised with in the world, to the extent that one of you, when he meets his brother, kisses him in the place of the light from his forehead’.
en.sarwar: 1. Abu Ali al-Ash’ari has narrated from al-Hassan ibn Ali al-Kufi from ‘Ubays ibn Hisham from al-Husayn ibn Ahmad al-Minqari from Yunus ibn Zabyan from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
In you there is a light by which you are identified in this world. It is as such that even when one of you meets his brother (in belief) he kisses him at the place of light in his forehead.”
